name: Pitch Black
label: Revelation
lede: An Oakland punk band with a keyboard player and a cowbell, two albums on a label built on youth crew, and a closing song called Executives and Art Directors.

eras.title: Three hundred numbered copies
eras.text: Pitch Black came out of Oakland playing punk and rock and roll. A hand-numbered 7" on a local label got them started, and Revelation, then moving well past its straight edge roots, put out their debut album.

years.h: Pitch Black's debut 7" on Cheetah's Records
years.p: Three songs, Half Empty, Undefeated and No Leaders, hand-numbered out of 300 on black vinyl with a lyric insert.
The 300 numbered copies of Pitch Black's Cheetah's Records 7" go, and the label presses it again, on blood red and orange vinyl.

years.h: Pitch Black, the Oakland band's Revelation debut · REV 113
years.p: Eleven songs, from The Wrath to Funeral Notice, with Half Empty and Undefeated from the 7" and a song called Rock and Roll Girl. Revelation pressed 250 on purple and 850 on black.

years.h: Pitch Black land on Revelation's 2002 sampler
years.p: Pitch Black appear on the Revelation Records Sampler 2002, and again on the label's 2004 Collection (REV 110).

eras.title: The modern sound
eras.text: Pitch Black's second Revelation album added Jeremy Goody on keyboards and ran thirteen songs, with a two-part centerpiece and a closer called Executives and Art Directors.

years.h: This Is the Modern Sound · Revelation REV 124
years.p: Thirteen songs, opening with Tonopah, with Bronze Lady, Pt. 1 and Pt. 2 in the middle and Executives and Art Directors to close.
years.xp: Discogs credits Martin Munroe on bass, vocals and guitar, Kevin Cross on guitar, vocals and "propaganda", Jamie Morrison on drums and cowbell, and Jeremy Goody on keyboards.

years.h: Pitch Black on Revelation's A Few Ditties From sampler
years.p: Revelation includes Pitch Black on its 2005 sampler, Revelation Records Presents A Few Ditties From.
